manifest.arithmetic_scope: symbolic Banach-space chain rule, operator-valued method-of-steps time-smoothing induction, parameterized scalar implicit-function theorem, section-chart adapter, and isolated-section semiflow stable-set identification only; no model-specific numerical ingress

runtime.arithmetic: formal theorem text and exact JSON/SHA-256 binding; no floating-point or model-specific numerical arithmetic

direct_return_stable_set_lemma.C2_graph_consequence: only if Q is C2, p is its hyperbolic fixed point, and DQ(p) has the required splitting does a stable graph theorem for Q construct this same periodic-orbit stable-set germ
direct_return_stable_set_lemma.Q_equals_Pm_route: Q=P^m on suitable nested domains is a sufficient algebraic way to identify the same germ
direct_return_stable_set_lemma.discrete_stable_set_definition: W_N^s(Q)={x in N: Q^n(x) is in N for all n and Q^n(x)->p}
direct_return_stable_set_lemma.exact_local_equality: W_N^s(Q)=N intersect W_G^s(Gamma) under the displayed domain and tube hypotheses
direct_return_stable_set_lemma.flow_stable_set_definition: W_G^s(Gamma)={x: Phi_t(x) is in G for all t>=0 and dist(Phi_t(x),Gamma)->0}
direct_return_stable_set_lemma.forward_implication: Q^n(x)->p implies dist(Phi_t(x),Gamma)->0 because every large t lies on a uniformly bounded flow arc issuing from Q^n(x), and joint continuity is uniform on that compact time band
direct_return_stable_set_lemma.intervening_tube: there is one common local tube G such that Phi_s(x) belongs to G for every x in N and 0<=s<=Theta(x)
direct_return_stable_set_lemma.reverse_implication: flow convergence gives dist(Q^n(x),Gamma)->0 at t_n; since Q^n(x) remains in N, compactness of Gamma and the isolated section closure force Q^n(x)->p
direct_return_stable_set_lemma.section_isolation: the closure of N meets Gamma only at p; equivalently for the proof, y_n in N and dist(y_n,Gamma)->0 imply y_n->p
direct_return_stable_set_lemma.selected_return_domain: Theta:N->[Theta_lower,Theta_upper] and Q:N->N are continuous, 0<Theta_lower<=Theta_upper<infinity, Q(x)=Phi_{Theta(x)}(x), Theta(p)=m*P for an integer m>=1, and Q(p)=p
direct_return_stable_set_lemma.selected_times: t_0=0 and t_n=sum_{j=0}^{n-1} Theta(Q^j(x)); the positive lower bound gives t_n->infinity and the upper bound covers each interval [t_n,t_{n+1}] by one uniformly bounded arc
direct_return_stable_set_lemma.setting: Phi is a continuous semiflow on a metric phase space, Gamma is a compact P-periodic orbit, p belongs to Gamma, and N is a local section patch containing p
direct_return_stable_set_lemma.stable_set_germ: germ_p W^s(Q)=germ_p(Sigma intersect W^s(Gamma)) after shrinking isolated section patches N

event_and_return_derivative_formulas.affine_section_specialization: if g is affine then D2g=0, recovering the usual event-aligned variational formula
event_and_return_derivative_formulas.notation: set S(t,u)=Phi_t(iota(u)); evaluate S, H=g o S and their partial derivatives at (T(u),u); h,k are directions in M

eventual_time_smoothing_lemma.C1_base: fixed-time Volterra differentiation gives D_phi Phi_t; for t>tau_star the translated arbitrary initial-history piece has cleared the complete output segment, and the solution and first-variation integral equations give J_10 and J_01 continuously in X and L(X,X), respectively
eventual_time_smoothing_lemma.C2_conclusion: S restricted to Omega_2 is jointly Frechet C2 in (t,phi)
eventual_time_smoothing_lemma.C2_step: for s>tau_star the segment x_s is C1 and x''(s)=DF(x_s)[theta->x'(s+theta)]
eventual_time_smoothing_lemma.complete_segment_C2: if t>2*tau_star, then every s=t+theta in the output segment satisfies s>tau_star, so x'', first-variation time derivatives, and all second mixed jets are continuous over the complete theta interval
eventual_time_smoothing_lemma.induction_step: differentiate x'=F(x_t) and the triangular variational hierarchy; the highest pure spatial jet satisfies a linear Volterra variational equation with coefficient DF, whose inhomogeneous source is a finite Banach Faà di Bruno combination of D^qF and lower operator-valued jets; the mixed time jets follow by differentiating the equation; t>j*tau_star makes the earliest output time exceed (j-1)*tau_star, so the lower-jet induction applies on the whole segment; local Volterra estimates give continuity in multilinear operator norm
eventual_time_smoothing_lemma.joint_Frechet_Ck_conclusion: S restricted to Omega_k is C^k jointly in time and initial history
eventual_time_smoothing_lemma.locality: at each base point, a compact trajectory-time interval and a sufficiently small solution neighborhood give the local Volterra bounds needed for Frechet C^k regularity; no global uniform derivative bound over an unbounded D is asserted
eventual_time_smoothing_lemma.operator_jet_space: J_ab(t,phi)=partial_t^a D_phi^b Phi_t(phi) belongs to L^b(X,X), with L^0(X,X)=X and a+b<=k
eventual_time_smoothing_lemma.operator_norm_induction_statement: for every 1<=j<=k and a+b<=j, J_ab exists and is continuous in the norm of L^b(X,X) on Omega_j; this is the induction statement that yields joint Frechet C^j
eventual_time_smoothing_lemma.proof_style: operator-valued method-of-steps induction, the Volterra variational hierarchy, and the Banach chain rule; no dimension-dependent estimate enters
eventual_time_smoothing_lemma.strict_boundary: the inequality is strict to avoid propagated compatibility faces at integer combinations of delays

fixed_time_initial_data_smoothness.key_distinction: varying t moves the translated evaluation point, whereas varying phi at fixed t does not
fixed_time_initial_data_smoothness.proof_mechanism: differentiate the Volterra integral equation in the initial history; the first and higher jets solve the triangular retarded variational hierarchy
fixed_time_initial_data_smoothness.statement: on every common existence tube contained in U, for each fixed t the segment solution operator Phi_t:phi->x_t(phi) has the same C^k initial-history smoothness as F, 1<=k<=r
fixed_time_initial_data_smoothness.unadvanced_history_piece: for t<tau_star, part of Phi_t(phi) is a fixed translation of phi and is affine, hence harmless for fixed-t differentiation

minimum_application_certificate.A_equation: finite d, finite constant delays, F in C^k
minimum_application_certificate.B_semiflow_domain: the parameterized initial histories and common event window belong to the open maximal semiflow domain Omega
minimum_application_certificate.D_initial_parameterization: a C^k map iota:D subset M->U from an open Banach coordinate domain
minimum_application_certificate.E_event_domain: V open in X, g:V->R in C^k, and Phi_t(iota(D)) subset V throughout the common window
minimum_application_certificate.F_event: two strict endpoint signs and one uniform positive speed
minimum_application_certificate.G_local_return_optional: to call the hit a section return, validate terminal section-chart containment and a C^k terminal inverse chart
minimum_application_certificate.H_ordinal_optional: earlier-event count/exclusion only if m-th or first-return semantics are claimed
minimum_application_certificate.I_stable_set_optional: for stable-germ identification validate Q:N->N, Q(p)=p, Theta(p)=mP, bounded positive return times, one intervening tube, and closure(N) intersect Gamma={p}

network_dimension_audit.delay_count: any finite number of fixed discrete delays
network_dimension_audit.network_encoding: a finite network with finitely many node coordinates is one larger vector x in R^d
network_dimension_audit.threshold_depends_on: only k and the maximum delay tau_star

nonautomaticity_example.conclusion: fixed-time smooth dependence does not make a variable-time complete-history map C2 on an open ball of arbitrary continuous histories
nonautomaticity_example.second_derivative_obstruction: differentiating again requires the derivative of phi at r-tau_star when both time directions are nonzero

ordinal_and_no_earlier_boundary.m_th_label: calling it the m-th admissible return additionally requires a directed count/exclusion of all earlier admissible events
ordinal_and_no_earlier_boundary.selected_branch: the signs and speed prove one unique event in the declared window, independent of all earlier events

phase_space_and_equation.constant_delay_scope: every finite system x'=f(x(t),x(t-tau_1),...,x(t-tau_N)) with fixed 0<=tau_j<=tau_star and f in C^r; the proof also applies to any C^r functional F on X
phase_space_and_equation.dimension: d is any positive finite integer
phase_space_and_equation.excluded_classes: state-dependent delays, neutral equations, infinite delays, and infinite-dimensional node state require separate proofs
phase_space_and_equation.functional_domain: F:U subset X -> R^d on an open set U
phase_space_and_equation.maximal_semiflow_domain: Phi:Omega->X is the maximal local semiflow, with Omega a relatively open subset of [0,infinity) x U; (t,phi) belongs to Omega exactly on the declared solution-existence domain

references_and_proof_status.classical_background: Diekmann, van Gils, Verduyn Lunel and Walther, Delay Equations (1995), Chapters VII.4 and XIV.3
references_and_proof_status.use_of_background: fixed-time RFDE smooth dependence and Poincare-map context; the operator-valued method-of-steps induction, threshold, parameterized selected-event composition, and isolated-section stable-germ proof are spelled out in this artifact

safe_Ck_extension.event_and_hit_conclusion: for open V, g in C^k, image containment, and the same signs/speed gate, T and the complete-history hit R are C^k
safe_Ck_extension.induced_return_conclusion: a C^k section return follows only after terminal section-chart containment and composition with its C^k inverse chart
safe_Ck_extension.induction: the highest order-j pure spatial jet solves its linear Volterra variational equation with an inhomogeneous Banach Faà di Bruno source built from lower jets; mixed time jets then use the equation on the complete segment; the earliest output time t-tau_star exceeds the order-(j-1) threshold when t>j*tau_star
safe_Ck_extension.joint_segment_conclusion: S(t,u)=Phi_t(iota(u)) is jointly C^k on I x D by the operator-valued smoothing lemma and the C^k chain rule
safe_Ck_extension.operator_valued_regularization: for every a+b<=j, partial_t^a D_phi^b Phi_t is continuous in L^b(X,X) on Omega_j, 1<=j<=k

selected_event_return_theorem.ambient_event_hit_specialization: for M=X and iota=id, R is an ambient selected-event hit map into g^{-1}(0); this alone does not make R a section self-map
selected_event_return_theorem.common_window: I=[T_minus,T_plus] for every u in D
selected_event_return_theorem.event_functional_domain: V is open in X, g:V->R belongs to C^k, and Phi_t(iota(u)) belongs to V for every (t,u) in I x D
selected_event_return_theorem.induced_section_return: if iota is a C^k chart of an initial section patch, the hit satisfies R(D) subset Sigma_out, and chi:Sigma_out->D_out is a C^k terminal section chart, then P=chi o R:D->D_out is the induced C^k selected section return
selected_event_return_theorem.parameter_domain: M is a Banach section-coordinate space, D is open in M, and iota:D->U is a C^k initial-history parameterization; the ambient specialization is M=X and iota=id
selected_event_return_theorem.selected_event_conclusion: there is exactly one T(u) in (T_minus,T_plus), and local implicit-function branches agree globally by uniqueness
selected_event_return_theorem.semiflow_domain_containment: (t,iota(u)) belongs to the open maximal semiflow domain Omega for every (t,u) in I x D
selected_event_return_theorem.speed_gate: partial_t H(t,u)>=a_star>0 for every (t,u) in I x D

theorem_boundary.not_proved_here: necessity or sharpness of k*tau_star, state-dependent or neutral extensions, a section return without terminal chart containment, stable-germ identification without section isolation, any concrete flow/event tube, event ordinal, graph, Hessian, crossing, biological control, routing, capture, or safety statement
theorem_boundary.proved_here: the general operator-valued eventual-smoothing lemma, the parameterized selected-event hit C2 theorem and safe Ck extension, exact event/hit chain rules, the conditional induced-section-return adapter, and the isolated-section direct-return stable-set identification lemma
